pages.page_title: Franciszek Sterczewski i Klaudia Jachira przeciw Berkowi w TK. Wyłom w KO - Wydarzenia w INTERIA.PL
pages.capture_answer: The KO member who did not back Maciej Berek is Franciszek Sterczewski, KO MP from Poznań. The body places him among KO non-voters; only Klaudia Jachira (KO) voted against, though the headline lists both as 'przeciw'. The quarrel: after the Sejm vote, fellow KO MP Bartosz Arłukowicz posted 'To jest wojna. I to nie czas na dylematy' and attacked him; Sterczewski replied 'Albo bronimy zasad, albo niczym się nie różnimy od tych, którzy je łamią'. Arłukowicz also wrote about 'Święczkowskiego' and needing 'twardych zawodników'. The Sejm then elected Berek with 226 votes in favour. Date: not in the returned text.

pages.page_title: Konkurs grantowy Funduszu Obywatelskiego finansowany ze środków norweskiej Nagrody Rafto pod Honorowym Patronatem RPO | Rzecznik Praw Obywatelskich
pages.capture_answer: Civic Fund (Fundusz Obywatelski) grant competition funded by the financial part of the 2018 Rafto Prize, awarded to RPO Adam Bodnar and the Biuro RPO; the Norwegian Rafto Foundation passed it to the Fund at the laureates' wish. All of it goes through this competition, in two areas: judicial independence in Poland, and rights of women and/or sexual minorities and/or migrants. Dates: page header 2018-12-21 and 2019-01-31; publication 2019-01-09; launch planned for early January 2019; applications until 31 January 2019 at 14:00; projects run to end of 2019. Budget: no sum given. Evaluation panel: none named. Honorary patronage: RPO. Results item (R003) dated 2019-03-01 in the 'Zobacz także' list.

pages.capture_answer: The prosecutor assigned to the coup notification after Michał Ostrowski is Małgorzata Szeroczyńska. The lede gives her as 'Zastępca Prokuratora Okręgowego w Warszawie prokurator Małgorzata Szeroczyńska'. pages.page_title: Pełny zapis przebiegu posiedzenia Komisji Sprawiedliwości i Praw Człowieka (nr 179)
pages.capture_answer: Sitting no. 179 of the Sejm Justice and Human Rights Committee (3 September 2026) heard candidates Maciej Berek and Artur Kotowski on druki 3005 and 3006. Chair Paweł Śliz (Polska2050). Berek was presented by Jarosław Urbaniak (KO), who is outside the committee and spoke as nominators' representative. Votes: on Jabłoński's recess motion, 'Głosowało 28 posłów: za było 9 posłów, przeciw było 19 posłów, wstrzymało się 0 posłów.' (M.P. 15); the motion was not adopted. Jaskulski's counter-motion (answers first) was put to a vote ('głosujemy nad wnioskiem formalnym'), but no result is in the text read. No vote on either candidacy appears in the text read; the unread tail may contain one. Questions put to Berek (M.P. 5-21): Wójcik (PiS) on the TK's existence, Tusk ties, the cooling-off law and publication; Karolewska (KO) on experience; Warchoł (PiS, M.P. 14) on State Tribunal liability under art. 198 and 'prawa ręka premiera'; Kaleta (PiS) on legislation and non-publication; Piekarska (KO) on oaths and restoring the TK; Jaskulski (KO) on trust; Ćwik (Centrum) on presidential interference under art. 131; Jabłoński (RozwojPlus) on legal-adviser years; Woś (PiS) on the cooling-off law; Tomczykiewicz (KO) on recusal (question only); Witczak (KO); Smoliński (PiS) on contracts, the drafted bill and oaths; Żukowska (Lewica) on the ECtHR Wałęsa judgment. Berek's answers (M.P. 18-21), verbatim: he cites the 6 March 2024 Sejm resolution and CJEU case C-448/23 (18 December); says the Święczkowski position has the same legal conditions as Przyłębska's; says the bill's standards should be applied evenly; describes first contact with Tusk as Senate deputy Marshal and a 2007 offer from Tusk to coordinate government legislation as RCL president; says the bill was prepared 'z ministrem Bodnarem'; says he is still a member of the Okręgowa Izba Radców Prawnych and would deregister if appointed. Discrepancy: Szrot (PiS) says Berek 'jest on oficjalnie ministrem' (present tense), while Urbaniak's CV says membership ran to August 2026 and Woś says he was dismissed a few weeks earlier. Cross-link: Kaleta and Smoliński, who questioned Berek, are on the 58-name PiS nominator list of print 2334 (R022). The chair said 'nie mogę zagłosować za tą kandydaturą' while praising Berek; the candidacy is not named in that sentence, but the context points to Berek.

pages.capture_request: Date and signatories of the Rafto call to freeze Norway Grants to the Ministry of Justice.
pages.fetch_note: Page text fetched (HTTP 200). No publication date appears in the page text or metadata, so the date is not stated. The linked appeal PDF (https://www.rafto.no/assets/documents/Letters-and-appeals/Full-letter-to-MFA-Norway.pdf) was also read (text returned, not a saved file). The PDF has no date line. Its 'Signed' block lists six organisations and no individuals. The page says the six 'Organized' the appeal; the PDF says the Rafto Foundation 'assisted' the ICJ Norway ad-hoc group. Page asks for a freeze of transfers 'to or via the Ministry of justice in Poland and entities dependent on the Ministry'; PDF request 2 asks for a freeze 'to the Justice Program', with conditions. Page and PDF name Zbigniew Ziobro as Minister of Justice, and the PDF names President Andrzej Duda; this sweep's brief lists Waldemar Żurek as Justice Minister. The PDF's latest dated reference is 21 December 2020, so the letter probably predates 2026 (inference only, not a stated date).

Signatories (PDF 'Signed' block; the page names the same six as organisers): International Commission of Jurists Norway; The Norwegian Judges Association; The Norwegian Bar Association; The Norwegian Helsinki Committee; Human Rights House Foundation; Rafto Foundation for Human Rights. No individual signatories are named. The appeal asks Norway's Foreign Minister Ina Marie Eriksen Søreide to freeze Norway Grants transfers to Poland's Ministry of Justice. Probable date (inference only): early 2021, from the PDF's latest dated reference of 21 December 2020.

Its verbatim text, up to character 39,379 of 66,372, contains the item 22 section (heading 'Wybór sędziego Trybunału Konstytucyjnego (druki nr 3005, 3006, 3057 i 3058)'), the presentations, the debate and vote no. 14. The rest came back only as a condensed summary, which says item 22 and prints 3005, 3006, 3057 and 3058 are absent; the verbatim text contradicts that, so the verbatim text is relied on. Speech texts sit on separate per-speaker pages not fetched; only speaker names and club labels appear here. Czarzasty's party is not shown on the page. The page gives no biography of Maciej Berek or Artur Kotowski. Tusk and Żurek spoke later, on item 17 (crypto-asset act), not item 22. pages.capture_answer: The transcripts/164 page is a written declaration (tekst niewygłoszony) by Poseł Włodzimierz Czarzasty, dated 4 Sep 2026. It says that, through an error in vote no. 14 at 10:25 in item 22 (election of a Constitutional Tribunal judge), he marked no candidate, and that he intended to vote for Maciej Berek. The linked sitting transcript shows the item 22 debate and vote: Berek, presented by Poseł Jarosław Urbaniak for KO-club MPs, got 226 votes; Artur Kotowski, presented by Poseł Kazimierz Smoliński for the PiS club, got 184; 437 MPs voted and the absolute majority was 219. Berek was elected. Speakers are listed by name only; their speech texts were not fetched.

pages.page_title: Sylwia Gregorczyk-Abram i Adam Borowski. To oni zmierzą się o fotel RPO
pages.capture_answer: Nominator: the article does not name any MP, club or body that formally nominated Adam Borowski. It says only that he is 'kandydat popierany przez PiS' (a candidate supported by PiS). By contrast, Sylwia Gregorczyk-Abram's candidacy was submitted by 'posłowie KO i Lewicy'. What he does: a PRL-era democratic opposition activist, publisher and social activist who 'od wielu lat kieruje warszawskim Klubem Gazety Polskiej' (has for many years headed the Warsaw Gazeta Polska club), co-created Oficyna Wydawnicza Volumen, and was involved in the Komitet Polska-Czeczenia. At the end of March 2026 he was given a final six-month prison sentence for not complying with rulings ordering an apology to Roman Giertych.

pages.capture_answer: Only second-hand; it is not a grant list. The release (March 09, 2026) cites two ties: that the Free Courts Foundation received a $130,000 grant from the Open Society Foundations in 2023, according to the OSF website, and that Free Courts lists the National Endowment for Democracy as a 'partner organization' on its website. Wawrykiewicz is described only as a 'Polish lawyer' who co-founded Free Courts and sits on the board of DemoCrisis; no MEP role or party is stated. pages.page_title: The Polish National Foundation to launch its “Fair Courts” campaign abroad
pages.capture_answer: The foundation is the Polish National Foundation, not Free Courts, and the page gives no Polish-language name. Its Fair Courts campaign cost, in the vice president's words, just over 8 million zlotys. The article says the foundation's initial capital and activities were financed by sixteen Treasury-owned companies (PLN 185 million). Minister Piotr Gliński is its government supervisor. The one US element is a payment from the foundation to the Washington firm White House Writers Group ($45,000 a month plus expenses, registered under FARA, contract signed 13 October). No US government money to the foundation or to Free Courts is named, and there is no NED or Wawrykiewicz link.

pages.capture_answer: Article dated 13 Feb 2025. It says Poland's Liberal and left-leaning civil society organisations appealed to the Tusk-led government to make good a shortfall tied to USAID cuts (headline: 'USAID cuts compensation'), but names no signatory. pages.page_title: Controversial Poland NGO Funding Bill Becomes Law
pages.capture_answer: Context on Polish NGO funding rules. This LibertiesEU article, dated October 16, 2017, reports that Poland's president signed a bill on NGO funding and that the law creates the National Freedom Institute, which will control distribution of public funds from the government and the EU among Poland's 100,000 NGOs. International human rights organisations and a coalition of domestic NGOs had asked President Andrzej Duda (the page states no party for him) to veto it. The article says the bill 'may be used to undercut groups with missions that conflict with the ruling party's positions'. It names none of the listed organisations, no EU programme beyond the general reference to EU public funds, no US funder, and no 2024-26 payment, so it cannot answer the lead question. The page links no 2024-26 source.

pages.page_title: Zapytanie w sprawie umowy nr MS/5286/DKO/2024 zawartej z Kancelarią Hoffman Taborowski i Wspólnicy Adwokacka Spółka Partnerska
pages.capture_answer: This page is the source of the firm mention. It is written question no. 3200 to the minister of justice ('do ministra sprawiedliwości'), headed 'Zapytanie w sprawie umowy nr MS/5286/DKO/2024 zawartej z Kancelarią Hoffman Taborowski i Wspólnicy Adwokacka Spółka Partnerska'. Author, verbatim: 'Zgłaszający: Dariusz Matecki, Zbigniew Ziobro'. Date, verbatim: 'Data wpływu: 20-02-2026' (date of receipt). The text says, 'W związku z zawarciem w dniu 25 listopada 2024 r. umowy nr MS/5286/DKO/2024 z Kancelarią...', that the contract was concluded with the firm for analysis and a recommendation on a legal opinion about judges' declarations to the Krajowa Rada Sądownictwa, for 4920,00 zł. It asks for the full contract with annexes, the scope and analysis, whether a separate opinion was prepared and by whom, the payment record, and who on the ministry side approved the work. No reply is included. On the lead question: the only public-body fee this page names is this 4920,00 zł contract with the ministry (alleged by the submitters). No foreign client and no other state client is named. No partner is named, and Maciej Taborowski is not mentioned; 'Taborowski' appears only in the firm's name. The question gives no register number. The firm name matches compabase's record for KRS 0000901486 by name only, and that record dates the addition of 'Taborowski' to 2026-04-01, after both the contract date and the receipt date.

pages.capture_answer: Reply dated 03 kwietnia 2026 r. from the Ministry of Justice, signed by Sekretarz Stanu Arkadiusz Myrcha and addressed to Marshal of the Sejm Włodzimierz Czarzasty. It answers 67 parliamentary queries from MP Dariusz Matecki, about 86 civil-law contracts (with annexes) the ministry concluded in 2024, as one collective reply. It says the ministry published registers of civil-law contracts for 2019–2023 and for 2024, and information on contracts concluded within the Justice Fund, but it names no contractor, firm, amount or fee. Hoffman, Taborowski i Wspólnicy is not named. The minister is referred to only as 'Minister Sprawiedliwości', and no other listed actor appears. The reply argues that the queries do not meet the rules for parliamentary queries and asks that this collective reply be accepted in place of separate replies. Footnote 1 cites related case numbers BK-VII.0520.87.2026 to BK-VII.0520.155.2026 without links.

pages.page_title: UCHWAŁA TRYBUNAŁU KONSTYTUCYJNEGO z dnia 25 marca 1992 r. (W. 2/92)
pages.capture_answer: The lead question is not resolved. This PDF is not the Constitutional Tribunal Act. It is the Tribunal's resolution of 25 March 1992 (W. 2/92; Dz.U. 1992 Nr 36 poz. 159) on arts 23(1), 26 and 28(1)(2) of the Act on Legal Advisers of 6 July 1982. Its holding: entry on the legal advisers' list of a person practising as a judge or prosecutor is inadmissible. Remigiusz Orzechowski's separate opinion (6 April 1992) disagrees, and reads art. 26 as banning only simultaneous practice. Maciej Taborowski and the other 2026 actors are not named. The resolution cites the Constitutional Tribunal Act of 29 April 1985 only as its procedural basis and reproduces none of its text, so the TK Act's other-activity rules are not answered here. The TK Act itself would need to be located and read; no link to it is on this page.

pages.capture_answer: Year: 2025. Session 'The rule of law and justice system', 23 April 2025, 12:30-14:00, Conference Room 6, 'Session translated simultaneously PL/EN'. Edition number: not stated; the sidebar names the 2027 edition 'XIX European Economic Congress'. The city appears only in the meta keywords ('EEC POLAND Katowice, EKG'). Speakers (six, under 'Speakers'): Łukasz Bernatowicz; Robert Gwiazdowski; Piotr Kamiński; Krystian Markiewicz (President, Association of Polish Judges "Iustitia"); Maciej Nowicki (Chairman of the Board, Helsinki Foundation for Human Rights); Katarzyna Stabińska (Partner, Ślązak, Zapiór i Partnerzy - Kancelaria Adwokatów i Radców Prawnych sp.p.). Who invited the panellists: not stated on this page; the Congress Programme Committee page failed with a client error and was not read. Partners and sponsors: not on this page; see R113-link1.
